title: Sonic Jelly Fox & BoomBox Resonance Lab
description: A soft-body Fox made of translucent jelly sits on a platform beside a BoomBox. The user adjusts frequency, amplitude, and bass boost knobs on the BoomBox to emit visible sound waves that deform the Fox's mesh in real time. The goal is to sculpt the Fox into specific silhouette targets while obeying energy conservation — total deformation energy is finite and redistributed, not created. Full undo/redo support tracks every knob change.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing a soft-body sound-wave deformation lab. Load BoomBox.glb scaled to 1.5 units on the left side and Fox.glb scaled to 2 units on the right side of a circular platform. Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0,3,7) looking at origin, with OrbitControls. Lighting: warm DirectionalLight from upper-left, soft AmbientLight, and a pulsing PointLight on the BoomBox that syncs with output intensity. Make the Fox's geometry soft-body: on load, clone its mesh vertices into a spring-mass system storing rest positions and velocities. Each vertex acts as a mass-spring node connected to neighbors with damping. The BoomBox has three virtual knobs rendered as HTML range sliders overlaid on screen: Frequency (1-20 Hz), Amplitude (0-1), and Bass Boost (0-1). When any knob changes, emit concentric ring wave meshes from the BoomBox toward the Fox. Waves apply forces to Fox vertices based on distance falloff and frequency. Implement energy conservation: total kinetic+potential deformation energy is capped at a constant. If amplitude increases, bass boost auto-attenuates proportionally, coupling the inputs. Update the spring-mass simulation each frame with Verlet integration, clamping displacement to max 0.5 units. Display a real-time energy bar (kinetic in red, potential in blue) as an HTML overlay. Implement an undo/redo stack (minimum 14 states) that records each knob adjustment as a snapshot of all three knob values plus vertex positions. Bind Ctrl+Z for undo and Ctrl+Y for redo, restoring Fox deformation and knob positions. Add a subtle wireframe overlay on the Fox toggled by pressing W to visualize the spring network. The Fox should gently wobble back toward rest shape when knobs are zeroed, showing viscous damping. The BoomBox speaker cone should visually pulse using a sine-scaled morph on its front face geometry. Render the platform as a glossy dark disc with MeshStandardMaterial and environment reflection.
